Game Setup

1. To determine the topography of the battlefield, each player rolls one die and adds the invasion rating of his army to the roll.  The total is the player's invasion score.  Each die is a specific color for a single player, displayed on the bottom of the screen. The highest invasion score is the invader; the defender must choose the battlefield topography from those in his army list.  Ties must be re-rolled.

2. Spawn the table based on the appropriate topography.  Click "Spawn table" in the control panel.

3. To determine which player has the tactical advantage, each player rolls one die and adds the maneuver rating of his army to the roll.  The total is the player's maneuver score.  The player with the higher maneuver score has the tactical advantage.  The difference in scores is the advantage score.  The advantage score is always 0 if it was necessary to re-roll a tie.

4. As part of the maneuver roll, if a player's unmodified roll is less than his army's maneuver rating or it equals 1, his army may perform a flank march.  Use the player's first roll if it was necessary to reroll a tie.

5. The number of terrain pieces to place on the table is determined by the terrain score.  Each player rolls one die.  Add the rolls together to obtain the terrain score.  The player with tactical advantage may then modify the terrain score by any amount equal to or less than his advantage score.  The advantage score may be added to or subtracted from the terrain score.  However, the modified terrain score may not be less than 2 or more than 12.  Please consult the Terrain Score Table.

6. The player with the tactical advantage selects the appropriate number of terrain pieces from the available terrain bags and then arranges the selected pieces in order, numbering the terrain pieces 1 through n (where n is the number of terrain pieces).  

7.  The player with the tactical advantage selects a terrain card at random and chooses which base edge of the card corresponds to his base edge.  Make sure to click the "Show deployment rulers" select box in the control panel displayed on the right of the screen.  The player then places all of the selected terrain pieces (including any stream or coast) on the game board.

8. When terrain placement is finished, right click the table and click "Fix terrain and lock".  Right click again to rotate to board if needed.

9. Each player in turn clicks on "Deploy an army" in the control panel. Select theme, select the army and the appropriate color. On some armies with models, the textures and flags are different! Bases with models spawn with the visual look of the topography type. You can toggle deployment lines for spawning with the "Show deployment rulers" select box in the control panel.

10. Now troops should be deployed. The player with tactical disadvantage places his camp, and then the player with tactical advantage does the same. Camps must be on the player's edge, normally within the center quadrant.

11. The disadvantaged player deploys his center deployment troops (at least 24 points), and may reserve troops for a flank march if eligible.

12. The advantaged player deploys all his troops, following all rules for center deployment. He may reserve troops for a flank march if eligible as well.

13.  The disadvantaged player deploys the remainder of his troops, and again may reserve troops for a flank march if eligible.

14.  The advantaged player takes the first turn of the game!

15. Selecting stands and other objects should be done by a single player. When selecting stands a future position will appear. A player may alter distance moved with the slider in the control panel. Clicking on the move button will move them.  If the results were not intended, feel free to use the undo button to restore the battlefield to a previous position.

16. Bases will snap in certain positions. Furthermore, when moving less than 0.2 MUs, they will go back to the original position.  Keep in mind that you may turn off and on snap to bases in the control panel.

17. Grabbing and moving a single stand will display how many MU it is moving as it is dragged across the table, taking into account rotations as well.  Incremental movement distance is displayed in the chat box for player reference.

18. Selecting several bases and clicking on "Wheel Group" in the control panel will spawn a new wheeling menu.  On this menu a player can control the direction and angle of the wheel, and either accept or cancel the move depending on the displayed MU cost.

19. Destroy your enemies, and fight for the glory of your nation!  Good luck.

These are all texts you can write in the chatbox, and the game will detect them, useful for specific features and mostly debugging

!triumph_help
Prints a brief help of all the commands.

!triumph_print_state
Prints all the current specials vars, in case the bases are not detected or the table.

!triumph_reset
Recalculates the main table by looking for objects of a Triumph! table size, and for bases using "starts with base and size is 40x15,20,30,40, 60 or 80" as criteria".

!triumph_debug
Toggles the debug mode. In this mode there's more printing to the chat log and there could be degraded performance, so use it only when checking some problem.
